verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.99
10. Kakudhavagga
Sīhasutta
“Sīho, bhikkhave, migarājā sāyanhasamayaṁ āsayā nikkhamati;
verses.english: “Mendicants, towards evening the lion, king of beasts, emerges from his den,

verses.pali: āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhati;
vijambhitvā samantā catuddisaṁ anuviloketi;
samantā catuddisaṁ anuviloketvā tikkhattuṁ sīhanādaṁ nadati;
verses.english: and roars his lion’s roar three times.

verses.pali: tikkhattuṁ sīhanādaṁ naditvā gocarāya pakkamati.
verses.english: Then he sets out on the hunt.

verses.pali: So hatthissa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
verses.english: If he strikes an elephant, he does it carefully, not carelessly.

verses.pali: mahiṁsassa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
gavassa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
dīpissa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
khuddakānañcepi pāṇānaṁ pahāraṁ deti antamaso sasabiḷārānampi, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ.
verses.english: or any smaller creatures—even a hare or a cat—he does it carefully, not carelessly.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
‘Mā me yoggapatho nassā’ti.
verses.english: Thinking: ‘May I not lose my way.’

verses.pali: Sīhoti kho, bhikkhave, tathāgatassetaṁ adhivacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa.
verses.english: ‘Lion’ is a term for the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tathāgato parisāya dhammaṁ deseti, idamassa hoti sīhanādasmiṁ.
verses.english: When the Realized One teaches Dhamma to an assembly, this is his lion’s roar.

verses.pali: Bhikkhūnañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
verses.english: When the Realized One teaches the monks …

verses.pali: bhikkhunīnañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
upāsakānañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
upāsikānañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
puthujjanānañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti antamaso annabhāranesādānampi, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ.
verses.english: or ordinary people—even food-carriers and hunters—he teaches them carefully, not carelessly.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
Dhammagaru, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammagāravo”ti.
verses.english: Because the Realized One has respect and reverence for the teaching.”

verses.pali: Navamaṁ.
